title: The iu8 risk multiplier reaches production only via --override, and cuts the repair queue 3.403x
verdict: the production profile pins the multiplier to 4.0 and silently discards a caller value; applied correctly, 1.0 cuts the repaired-row share 3.403x, confirming the gate's 3.40x on the production path for the first time
quant: mixed GGUF: Q4_K gate/up experts, Q5_1 down experts, Q5_K 2 tensors, Q8_0 5 tensors

defect.why_a_shell_value_is_discarded: qwen4_exp_profiles.py:638 _apply_profile_env writes os.environ[key] = value unconditionally. The binder records the discard in _last_prebinder_conflicts and _report_prebinder_conflicts() warns, but PREBINDER_CONFLICT_ENV defaults to 'warn', not 'error', so a discarded override is a log line and the run proceeds with the profile value.
defect.consequence: Every production and canonical A/B of this multiplier compared 4.0 against 4.0. The flat repair time, flat risk-owner time and flat window total reported from those runs are a property of the harness, not of the kernel.

the_working_path.why: scripts/qwen4exp_profile_gap.py:419-430 applies overrides after the profile binder has run, then re-reads the effective environment.
the_working_path.self_proving: Each run records bound_route_env (post-binder, pre-override) and route_env (effective), so an arm can be shown to have taken effect rather than assumed.

command: python3 scripts/qwen4exp_profile_gap.py --model-root /home/lhl/models/gguf/unsloth-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL/UD-Q4_K_XL --mode prefill --case-id code-p4096 --execution-profile production --risk-diagnostics --override HIPENGINE_QWEN4_EXP_Q4_IU8_RISK_MULT=<4.0|1.0> --compiler-version-file /tmp/hipengine-hipcc-version.txt --require-cached-build --output ovr-<mult>.json

result.agreement: The 3.403x measured here matches the 3.40x the gate harness recorded (repair share 0.7119% -> 0.2092% over 1504 calls and 9.86e9 outputs). This is the first independent confirmation of that figure on the production path.
result.note: The arm identity is proven by bound=4.0 / effective=1.0, not assumed from the shell.

open_question: Whether the repair TIME follows the queue. The repair kernel's grid-stride loop bound is min(risk_count, max_risks), so proportional work predicts 4808.702 ms -> ~1414 ms, a saving of ~3394 ms = 5.2% of the prefill window. The trace that decides it is running (bg-34), at both multipliers, both through --override.
note_on_the_3394_ms: The same ~3394 ms magnitude was derived in an earlier iteration from a fixed-grid mechanism that was subsequently withdrawn as a units error, and then from a flat-time premise that this artifact shows was an artifact of the pin. The magnitude is recorded here only as a prediction to be tested, not as a result.
limits: One host (gfx1151 APU), one model, one quant, one case (code-p4096), one execution profile.
--risk-diagnostics synchronizes the stream per call, so these runs are for the queue count and the arm identity, not for a timing claim.
No correctness gate applies: no arithmetic changed and no default was modified.
